title: Service bulletin SD-13-4860
text: Service Data - Bendix® WS-24™ Antilock Wheel Speed Sensor DESCRIPTION The Bendix® WS-24™ Wheel Speed Sensor (WSS) is an electromagnetic device used to obtain vehicle speed information for an antilock controller. When the wheel rotates, the sensor and an exciter ring (sometimes called a “rotor” or “tone” ring) generate a simple AC signal. This signal is sent to either the brake controller (Bendix® EC-60™ or Bendix® EC-80™) or the Global Scalable Brake Control electro-pneumatic modulator (Bendix® GSBC® EPM-90™), which analyzes the data and commands the Antilock Braking System (ABS) accordingly. Specifically, the WSS consists of a coil, pole piece, and a magnet. The exciter ring is a steel ring or gear-like device that has regularly spaced high and low spots called “teeth.” The WSS is mounted in a fixed position, while the exciter ring is installed on a rotating member (typically part of the hub) so that its “teeth” move, in close proximity, past the tip of the sensor. The WS-24 WSS is available in both straight and 90° versions to accommodate axle/wheel space limitations.

title: Service bulletin SD-13-4860
text: Service Data - Bendix® WS-24™ Antilock Wheel Speed Sensor DESCRIPTION The Bendix® WS-24™ Wheel Speed Sensor (WSS) is an electromagnetic device used to obtain vehicle speed information for an antilock controller. When the wheel rotates, the sensor and an exciter ring (sometimes called a “rotor” or “tone” ring) generate a simple AC signal. This signal is sent to either the brake controller (Bendix® EC-60™ or Bendix® EC-80™) or the Global Scalable Brake Control electro-pneumatic modulator (Bendix® GSBC® EPM-90™), which analyzes the data and commands the Antilock Braking System (ABS) accordingly. Specifically, the WSS consists of a coil, pole piece, and a magnet. The exciter ring is a steel ring or gear-like device that has regularly spaced high and low spots called “teeth.” The WSS is mounted in a fixed position, while the exciter ring is installed on a rotating member (typically part of the hub) so that its “teeth” move, in close proximity, past the tip of the sensor. The WS-24 WSS is available in both straight and 90° versions to accommodate axle/wheel space limitations.

title: Service bulletin SD-13-4860
text: Service Data - Bendix® WS-24™ Antilock Wheel Speed Sensor DESCRIPTION The Bendix® WS-24™ Wheel Speed Sensor (WSS) is an electromagnetic device used to obtain vehicle speed information for an antilock controller. When the wheel rotates, the sensor and an exciter ring (sometimes called a “rotor” or “tone” ring) generate a simple AC signal. This signal is sent to either the brake controller (Bendix® EC-60™ or Bendix® EC-80™) or the Global Scalable Brake Control electro-pneumatic modulator (Bendix® GSBC® EPM-90™), which analyzes the data and commands the Antilock Braking System (ABS) accordingly. Specifically, the WSS consists of a coil, pole piece, and a magnet. The exciter ring is a steel ring or gear-like device that has regularly spaced high and low spots called “teeth.” The WSS is mounted in a fixed position, while the exciter ring is installed on a rotating member (typically part of the hub) so that its “teeth” move, in close proximity, past the tip of the sensor. The WS-24 WSS is available in both straight and 90° versions to accommodate axle/wheel space limitations.

title: Service bulletin SD-13-4860
text: Service Data - Bendix® WS-24™ Antilock Wheel Speed Sensor DESCRIPTION The Bendix® WS-24™ Wheel Speed Sensor (WSS) is an electromagnetic device used to obtain vehicle speed information for an antilock controller. When the wheel rotates, the sensor and an exciter ring (sometimes called a “rotor” or “tone” ring) generate a simple AC signal. This signal is sent to either the brake controller (Bendix® EC-60™ or Bendix® EC-80™) or the Global Scalable Brake Control electro-pneumatic modulator (Bendix® GSBC® EPM-90™), which analyzes the data and commands the Antilock Braking System (ABS) accordingly. Specifically, the WSS consists of a coil, pole piece, and a magnet. The exciter ring is a steel ring or gear-like device that has regularly spaced high and low spots called “teeth.” The WSS is mounted in a fixed position, while the exciter ring is installed on a rotating member (typically part of the hub) so that its “teeth” move, in close proximity, past the tip of the sensor. The WS-24 WSS is available in both straight and 90° versions to accommodate axle/wheel space limitations.

title: Service bulletin SD-13-4860
text: Service Data - Bendix® WS-24™ Antilock Wheel Speed Sensor DESCRIPTION The Bendix® WS-24™ Wheel Speed Sensor (WSS) is an electromagnetic device used to obtain vehicle speed information for an antilock controller. When the wheel rotates, the sensor and an exciter ring (sometimes called a “rotor” or “tone” ring) generate a simple AC signal. This signal is sent to either the brake controller (Bendix® EC-60™ or Bendix® EC-80™) or the Global Scalable Brake Control electro-pneumatic modulator (Bendix® GSBC® EPM-90™), which analyzes the data and commands the Antilock Braking System (ABS) accordingly. Specifically, the WSS consists of a coil, pole piece, and a magnet. The exciter ring is a steel ring or gear-like device that has regularly spaced high and low spots called “teeth.” The WSS is mounted in a fixed position, while the exciter ring is installed on a rotating member (typically part of the hub) so that its “teeth” move, in close proximity, past the tip of the sensor. The WS-24 WSS is available in both straight and 90° versions to accommodate axle/wheel space limitations.

title: Owner complaint 11761919: HYUNDAI SANTA FE HYBRID 2025
text: The contact owns a 2025 Hyundai Santa Fe. The contact stated that while driving 40 MPH, the instrument panel went blank. The contact was able to pull over safely after the failure. The contact associated the failure with NHTSA Campaign Number: 26V047000 (Electrical System); however, the VIN was not include in the recall. The dealer was contacted by phone. The manufacturer was contacted by phone and made aware of the failure. The failure mileage was approximately 7,900.

title: Owner complaint 11761698: BMW X5 2026
text: Driving on highway using assisted driving pro (hands off steering wheel and feet off pedals). Speed set for 65 or 67. Driver's phone call came up on display screen. Passenger answered and hung up on screen. Driver did not touch wheel. Car started accelerating. Reached 93 mph before realized what was happening and able to apply brakes. Short time later tried to reengage speed and verbally requested increase to 65 or 67. Car set cruise control to 110. Both passengers heard 65 or 67, definitely not 110. Applied brake and didn't use any driver assistance controls for remainder of trip. Nice weather, no glare, light traffic. Software update was installed the day before. BMW dealership found no problem. National BMW consumer line suggested setting speed manually with buttons on steering wheel instead of verbally.

title: Owner complaint 11766326: HIGHLAND RIDGE FW HIGHLANDER 2019
text: The contact owns a 2019 Highland Ridge Highland RV. The contact stated that while driving 60 MPH and hauling the travel trailer, the axle weld and frame fractured. The contact was unable to pull the trailer. The contact stated that the road was bumpy while driving. The vehicle was towed. There was a fire within the axle three years prior. Lippert Industries, the manufacturer, was contacted by phone. The insurance company inspected the trailer and determined there was a manufacturer defect. An appointment was scheduled but it was uncertain that the RV was repairable.
